headline: DEA's 2026 quota update holds marijuana; Schedule III still unset
dek: A DEA notice published on 25 November 2026 raises psilocybin and gives HHC its own quota, but the Schedule III medical marijuana numbers are still to come.
key_points: DEA's proposed 2026 quota adjustments, published in the Federal Register on 25 November, leave Schedule I marijuana at 6,675 kg and marijuana extract at 1,000 kg.
Seven months after medical marijuana moved to Schedule III, DEA says it is still working out how to estimate legitimate need and will publish those quotas separately.
Hexahydrocannabinol (HHC) gets its own 30-gram quota after DEA gave it a separate drug code in May.
Psilocybin rises 20% to 60 kg and psilocyn about 17% to 93.6 kg, tied to the White House order on psychedelic treatments; comments close 28 December.
body: The Drug Enforcement Administration has proposed mid-year changes to how much of each Schedule I and II drug can be legally made in 2026, and the marijuana lines do not move. The notice, published in the Federal Register on 25 November 2026 under docket DEA-1568A, keeps the 2026 aggregate production quota for Schedule I marijuana at 6,675,000 grams, marijuana extract at 1,000,000 grams and delta-9-THC at 1,523,040 grams.

The more telling part is what is missing. Medical marijuana under a state licence moved to Schedule III in April, but DEA says it has still not set production quotas for the three new Schedule III drug codes. It is still registering the manufacturers and distributors who will handle them, and still choosing the data it will use to estimate national need.
## Why Schedule III still needs a quota

Most Schedule III drugs have no production quota. Marijuana is different because of an international treaty. The notice explains that the 1961 Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs requires licensed makers of drugs in its Schedule I, which includes marijuana, to work within quotas that stop production beyond legitimate need. The April final rule, published at 91 FR 22714 on 28 April 2026, wrote those controls in.

So DEA created three Schedule III drug codes, for marijuana, marijuana extract and naturally derived delta-9-THC in an FDA-approved product or covered by a state medical licence (codes 7362, 7353 and 7386). It says a separate Federal Register notice will propose quotas for them once the numbers are settled. Any marijuana outside those categories stays in Schedule I, under the existing codes and the unchanged quotas.

This is the second time this month DEA has said the same thing. As we reported on 9 November, its proposed 2027 quotas also held Schedule I marijuana at 6,675 kg and promised a separate Schedule III notice. Today's notice confirms there is still no date.
> Rescheduling changed the label on medical marijuana; the quota notice shows the supply rules behind it are still being written.

One cannabis change is new. In May, DEA gave hexahydrocannabinol, or HHC, a specific Schedule I listing and its own drug code (91 FR 23913, 4 May 2026). Registered manufacturers had previously received HHC quotas under the general tetrahydrocannabinols code. The notice now proposes a separate HHC quota of 30 grams for 2026, enough for analytical and research work, not commercial supply.

HHC has been sold in some hemp-derived products. Its separate listing gives DEA a cleaner way to track it, and it arrives as Congress fights over whether to delay the 11 December change to the federal hemp definition.

DEA also proposes a single 620-gram quota for 'cannabimimetic agents', a group of synthetic cannabinoids it consolidated under one drug code by a January rule. Two older compounds, JWH-018 and AM2201, keep their own codes.

The largest proposed increases are for psychedelics. Psilocybin goes from 50,000 to 60,000 grams, a 20% rise. Psilocyn goes from 80,000 to 93,600 grams, about 17%. Methylone (3,4-methylenedioxy-N-methylcathinone) goes from 30,000 to 42,500 grams, about 42%. DEA ties all three to manufacturer interest in dosage forms for clinical trials, following Executive Order 14401, which set a policy of speeding research and approvals for psychedelic treatments for serious mental illness.
Outside cannabis and psychedelics, the notice also raises several stimulant quotas. Lisdexamfetamine rises from about 51.3 million to 62.8 million grams.

For state-licensed medical operators, the missing Schedule III quota is not an immediate supply limit. DEA has registered more than 900 dispensaries since October, and nothing in today's notice limits them. But a quota will eventually cap how much medical marijuana DEA-registered growers can produce nationally. How DEA measures 'legitimate need', whether from state sales data, patient counts or something else, will decide whether that cap binds.

The supply chain is still contested in court. As we reported on 24 November, the Justice Department has asked the D.C. Circuit to deny a stay of DEA's medical marijuana supply-chain rule that takes effect on 29 November.

Comments on the 2026 adjustments are due by 28 December 2026 at regulations.gov, docket DEA-1568A, and the Administrator may hold a hearing. Watch for the separate notice proposing Schedule III marijuana quotas, the first time the federal government will put a national number on legal medical cannabis production. And watch 29 November, when the supply-chain rule is due to take effect.
